req.title: Task update persists
req.statement: The system shall persist PUT changes so subsequent GET requests reflect the update.

doc.reasoning: The test suite is designed to verify that the task update functionality in the FastAPI application correctly persists changes to the database. The tests cover positive, negative, and boundary cases to ensure robustness against common mutations such as operator flips, constant changes, and boolean negations.

tests.name: test_update_task_positive
preconditions: Task with id 1 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT request to update task with id 1
expected: Task title updated to 'Updated Task Title'
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Positive test: Update an existing task
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/1",
    json={"title": "Updated Task Title", "description": "Updated description", "completed": false}
)
assert response.status_code == 200
assert response.json()["title"] == "Updated Task Title"

tests.name: test_update_task_not_found
preconditions: Task with id 999 does not exist in the database
actions: Send PUT request to update non-existent task with id 999
expected: Error message 'Task with id 999 not found'
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Negative test: Update a non-existent task
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/999",
    json={"title": "Non-existent Task", "description": "This task does not exist", "completed": false}
)
assert response.status_code == 404
assert response.json()["detail"] == "Task with id 999 not found"

tests.name: test_update_task_boundary
preconditions: Task with id 20 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT request to update task with id 20
expected: Task title updated to 'Boundary Task Title'
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Boundary test: Update the last task in the pre-loaded data
response = client.put(
    "/tasks/20",
    json={"title": "Boundary Task Title", "description": "Boundary description", "completed": true}
)
assert response.status_code == 200
assert response.json()["title"] == "Boundary Task Title"
